description: `accounts lend <seat> off` writes seat-state.json persistently (a human's own toggle, kept outside config so it needs no edit/reload); a later dispatch --dry-run treats a lent-off seat exactly like a config-level outage — pulled from its chain as if not configured there at all — and falls to the next entry. Checked ahead of the breaker in accounts.py's `_availability` order (check 3), distinct from both `available = false` (dispatch-fallback-unavailable, a config edit) and a breaker trip (dispatch-breaker-open, machine-observed): this is the one human toggle that lives in state, not config.

home.config_toml:
[accounts.seat-a]
kind = "codex"
short = "sa"
config_dir_var = "CODEX_HOME"
config_dir = "{{DIR:codex-home-a}}"
pool = "codex:a"

[accounts.seat-b]
kind = "codex"
short = "sb"
config_dir_var = "CODEX_HOME"
config_dir = "{{DIR:codex-home-b}}"
pool = "codex:b"

[projects.sandbox]
path = "{{PROJECT:sandbox}}"

[projects.sandbox.chains]
explorer = ["seat-a", "seat-b"]

[roles.explorer]
write_scope = "none"
effort = "low"
on_exhausted = "degrade"
skills = []

[roles.explorer.models]
codex = "gpt-test"

stdout_contains: skipped     seat-a: lent off — not in chains right now (`accounts lend` to change it)
